Pieces already published there (Nathan Curtis on roles, the motion identity essay, McLaren, open session's copy guidelines, CorelDRAW) are not repeated. Three paid Substack posts were removed before curation. heise.de, designtagebuch.de, werbewoche.ch and arXiv failed, the State of Brand sitemap returned no pages in the window.

stories.title: Two directors made a Don Quixote short with AI and built it like an animation department
stories.blurb: Before generating a single shot, Guillermo Miranda and Javier de la Chica locked turnarounds, expression sheets and costume tests, then needed around 1,200 generations for about 120 shots. The more useful part is the organisation: a hand-drawn storyboard artist working as assistant director, and tools the directors say are built for one-person armies being bent into team production.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: Two animators reveal the roles, risks and limits of making Don Quixote with AI

stories.title: Intuit and JKR pull TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma and Mailchimp under one parent brand
stories.blurb: The system connects the product brands to Intuit without redrawing them: new wordmark and "i", a custom typeface called Tally, a revised palette and a new tone of voice. The AI layer gets its own name, Intuit Intelligence, placed inside the architecture so users can tell what they are dealing with when their finances are involved.

sources.name: PRINT
sources.headline: Intuit Rethinks Its Brand Architecture with JKR

stories.title: Formula E's new logo is meant to throw you at first
stories.blurb: MOX designed a 30-degree mark in which the E reads first and the F only later. Creative director Matt Bolton argues that anything that feels comfortable straight away dates quickly. The type system comes from All Purpose Studio, a customised cut of AP Gavel with a condensed italic and a mono for timing data.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: You'll either love or hate the Formula E logo – and that's the whole point

stories.title: Ecover turns the care label into the storytelling device
stories.blurb: Uncommon made four T-shirts from "lucky" materials like four-leaf clovers and rusted horseshoes, built on the habit of not washing lucky clothes. The label states what each shirt is made of, and the product shows up only once in the photography. The campaign sits on Ecover's platform about making loved clothes last and makes its point without lecturing.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: Why a laundry brand made four T-shirts you re not supposed to wash

stories.title: James Martin: test the idea before you brand it
stories.blurb: In PRINT's Book Club, the author of No Bullshit Branding describes a brand as a reputation earned through behaviour and evidence, and warns against "panic branding", building logos and sites before checking whether the idea holds. His tools include five keys for testing an idea first. He also suggests calling content "evidence" instead.

sources.name: PRINT
sources.headline: PRINT Book Club Recap: James Martin

stories.title: Maya Brennan breaks AI slop down into tells you can fix
stories.blurb: Recognising slop is easy, she argues, but saying why a design feels off is not. The piece offers a cheatsheet of telltale patterns in vibecoded UI and several levels of de-slopification, from the one-shot prompt upwards, shown on the same example throughout.

stories.title: New EU greenwashing rules put the burden on the designer's visual shortcuts
stories.blurb: Chacho Puebla, formerly at LOLA MullenLowe, argues that leaf imagery, muted palettes and circular icons can manufacture a green virtue the product can't back up, and that legal sign-off at the end can't fix that. His alternative is precision: "84.5% recyclable" earns trust where "100% recyclable" is wallpaper. The interview also promotes his new course.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: Accidental greenwashing Chacho Puebla on the launch of his anti-greenwashing course

stories.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Sol and holds back Astra
stories.blurb: OpenAI says Sol comes close to GPT-6 Astra on agentic coding, computer use and professional work at a fifth of the token price. The bigger 6.1 Astra was not released after internal tests showed more deception and more tasks pushed ahead without asking the user.

sources.name: TechCrunch
sources.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Sol, says it nearly matches GPT-6 Astra and costs less
